segments.text: Brain on beliefs, sheet on the wire I close my eyes, and there you stand
Young as the day we reach that land
Daddy Kemp let us inside his shirt
They made us laugh when the silence hurt
Taught me could find a trail through the green
Now they return in the things that I dream
Rode of blades beating the dawn into smoke
A radio whistler, a rifle bolt smoke
We counted the living when daylight was gone
And learned how the world could keep moving on
They cleaned up the map and called it a plan
With no line of ink through the heart of a man
I carry your names home
Through every mile I survived alone
No middle can absent, no flag can explain
Well, I saw the morning and you saw the rain
When memory calls me, I never let go
I carry your names home
Red earth clung hard to the soles of our fleet, smoke turned the moon to a merciless heat.
A village stood quiet, a doorway was bare, fear had a face and it lived everywhere.
We were sons with our voices still changing at night, told to be certain and ordered to
fight.
I remember the wounded, the frightened, the cries and the questions that stayed when the
gunfire went wild.
The years built a house where the old shadows roamed.
Some of us returned, but not all made it home.
I carry your name's home.
Through every mile I survived alone.
No metal can answer, no fact can explain.
Why I saw the morning and you saw the rain.
Whenever he calls me, I never let go.
I carry your name's home.
At the wall, my hand finds every letter, called Blackstone, but I hear you better.
Not as soldiers, frozen in flame, but as boys with a joke and a hometown name.
If you wanted children, where you wanted the sea, Tommy said, save the code one for me.
I kept that promise through forty long years, one glass for the laughter, one brass for the tears.
The world does not vanish when silence begins
It follows the living beneath their skin
So I speak for the friends who cannot grow old
Not for the glory, for the truth to be told
I carry your names home
You never want that dark road alone
No speech can return you, no anthem erase
The heat of that country, the light in your face
As long as I'm breathing, the whole world will know
I carry your names home
When my own evening comes and the last light is low
I follow your voices wherever they go
Till then every sun rise through sorrow and hope
I carry your names
I carry your name and soul.
